text:
jess_support: FYI ACME reported their embeddings suddenly changed shape for calls to /v1/embeddings. They expect 1536 but client sees 768. :confused:
customer_acme: reproducer attached — we call model=redwood-large-embed with text chunks, then index. Started this morning after a deploy. Latency also spiked to ~800ms.
andrew_oncall: can you paste the request headers (just region/host) and a sample response (dims)?
customer_acme: headers: 
  x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
  Authorization: Bearer ...
response snippet: {"model":"redwood-large-embed","embedding":[...768 floats...] }
jess_support: interesting — 768 suggests fallback to redwood-medium-embed or a 3rd-party variant. Checking routing logs now. :eyes:
devops_bot: capacity-alert: eu-west-1 embed pool at 96% for RESERVED_TIER, spilling to fallback pool. timestamp=2025-11-02T09:12:34Z
andrew_oncall: logs show request routed_to=us-east-1, fallback_reason=insufficient_capacity, model_variant=redwood-medium-embed. So despite x-redwood-region=eu-west-1 header, policy allowed cross-region redirect when reserved capacity exhausted. That explains dims and cold start latency.
maria_ml: that matches — redwood-large-embed has 1536 dims; redwood-medium-embed returns 768. When routing falls back to cheaper variant we need to surface that to customer or honor region pin.
customer_acme: Is there a quick workaround? Our app has strict EU residency requirement, cannot send embeddings outside eu-west-1.
jess_support: short-term: set routing_preference=region_strict in the request or pin model=redwood-large-embed@v123 (we can pin version + region). I'll send commands.
andrew_oncall: repro steps I used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "x-redwood-region: eu-west-1" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-embed","input":["test"]}'
```
Then check audit trace id header X-Redwood-Trace. In our route logs trace 8821 went to us-east-1 with fallback tag.
ops_sre: root cause: autoscaling failed to add additional capacity fast enough after a batch of long-lived KV-cache sessions. Batching spike from several customers saturated the eu pool. We saw cold starts in the fallback pool in us-east-1 which caused the ~800ms latency.
jess_support: Customer wants to avoid any cross-region fallback. I created a ticket to add a tenant-level flag to disable cross-region fallback. For now I'm sending this suggested change: routing_preference: "region_strict" in the JSON body.
customer_acme: tried that — got 429 with message "insufficient regional capacity" instead of being routed. That's acceptable for them (fail closed).
maria_ml: follow-up: we should also detect dim mismatch and return a clear API-level warning when fallback changes model dimensionality. Right now client just sees different vector length which is confusing.
andrew_oncall: agreed. Action items:
- ops_sre: prioritize scaling hotfix for eu embed pool (ETA 2h)
- infra: expose tenant setting to disable cross-region fallback (ETA 3d)
- api: return header X-Redwood-Fallback: <region/model> when fallback happens (ETA 1d)
- docs: add guidance for region_strict and pinning models (ETA today)

ops_sre: scaling hotfix deployed to eu pool, will monitor for 30m.
devops_bot: deploy: eu-embed-hotfix started by ops_sre at 2025-11-02T10:02:14Z
jess_support: customer confirmed they received 1536-dim responses again after hotfix and latency back to ~120ms. :tada:
customer_acme: confirm — looks good now. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
maria_ml: created a small PR to add a client warning when dims mismatch; includes suggestion to pin model or use region_strict.
andrew_oncall: closing loop: we'll add metric alert for cross-region fallback rate > 0.5% and a dashboard panel for embed-dim distribution per model.
jess_support: noted. I'll update the escalation ticket with repro steps, response headers, and the actions above. Closing thread unless anyone objects. :white_check_mark:
